title: Newton Basins of Orthogonal-Polynomial Approximants of Functions with a Jump Discontinuity: A Numerical Study of Root Location and Basin Complexity
content: Newton’s method cannot be applied directly to a function with a jump discontinuity, because the function has no derivative at the jump. We replace such a function by its polynomial approximant of degree N, orthogonal with respect to a Chebyshev-type weight with an exponential factor centred at the jump, and study numerically the Newton map of the approximant in the complex plane. We prove three elementary facts: the Newton map has degree N with a repelling fixed point at infinity; the normalised weight measure concentrates at the jump, not at the endpoints, as the damping parameter grows; and the roots of the approximant can be computed stably as eigenvalues of a comrade matrix. For three test functions and N≤30 we observe that the non-real roots approach the jump at a rate close to N−1, whereas for smooth controls they remain at distance of order one; that a single large real root occurs for only one of the three functions; and that the standard deviation σ(N) of Newton iteration counts, used as an indicator of basin complexity, grows roughly linearly with N, but equally or more strongly for smooth controls, so the growth is not specific to the discontinuity. The sensitivity of σ to the grid, tolerance and iteration cap is quantified. No asymptotic result is claimed.
